rationale: Both legs share the same numerator (che) and the two parent signals already deliver near-identical results (5.8%/t=5.08 and 5.3%/t=4.92), so averaging two ~collinear proxies is a cosmetic blend whose outcome is essentially predetermined and teaches nothing new about the mechanism.

Cash share of current assets is a highly persistent business-model characteristic, so a three-year moving average will correlate near-unity with the level already tested in LiquidCurrentAssetProfit — the "persistent vs transitory" decomposition claimed is not actually identified by this smoothing, and the only certain effect is a small coverage/turnover change.

This is the only proposal that brings a genuinely new information channel (cash-flow-statement total accruals) into the archive and its conversion-rate deflator is economically motivated and sign-consistent, though it sits close to the canonical Sloan accrual anomaly and the act−che deflator can approach zero for cash-rich firms, producing spurious top ranks.

A single-leg numerator swap is a modest step, and the archive's own evidence is discouraging (every oancf-margin leg tested — MarginCollectedInCash, PayablesStretchedCashProfit — produced negative alphas at coverage as low as 0.06), but the complement-versus-double-counting question it poses is legitimate and directly informs the final consolidation.

Internally consistent and a defensible dynamic extension of the realization channel that is distinct from the failed one-year delta, but a rising cash share is heavily contaminated by equity issuance and asset sales rather than earnings conversion, so the mechanism attribution will be ambiguous even if it works.

The structural diagnosis (additive gated form preserves the FMB slope that MIN/SUMRANK composites destroy) is correct and well-reasoned, but the signal is ProfitPlusConditionalLiquidityBonus with one extra z-score added to the bonus term, and the depreciation-conservatism channel has been inconsistent across its two archive tests, so this is an incremental extension rather than a new idea.
